# Art and sound are generated by the game's own code

Every sprite, texture, effect, sound, piece of music and spoken alert in Ironfront is produced at runtime by our own TypeScript: pixel art from compact templates and a single palette table, sounds from Web Audio recipes, music from a small seeded composer, and alerts through the browser's speech synthesis using only voices that are local to the computer. The repo holds no image, audio or font files and the game adds no dependency for them. We chose this over drawing art in an editor or using sound packs because it keeps everything original and free of licences, lets agents change and test the look like any other code, keeps the build to plain TypeScript (ADR 0001), and keeps every look-and-feel change a two-way door.

## Consequences

- The world is drawn as pixel art at 12 pixels per Cell into a low-resolution canvas and shown at 2x with smoothing off, so a Cell stays 24 screen pixels and camera, minimap and click maths do not change. Interface text stays sharp at full resolution.
- Art generators output plain pixel buffers (width, height, RGBA) and sound and music generators output plain data, so they run and are tested without a browser; a thin client layer turns them into canvases and audio. They run once at startup or when needed, never per frame for anything that does not change.
- All art colours live in one palette table (`src/client/art/artPalette.ts`); recolouring the game is an edit there.
- Code for art and sound lives in folders that the one-way door rules do not match: those rules treat any folder named `assets`, `sprites`, `audio`, `sound`, `sounds`, `music` or `fonts` as third-party assets. Use names such as `src/client/art/` and `src/client/sfx/`; file names do not matter.
- Nothing leaves the player's machine: no network calls for art, sound, music or voices, and spoken alerts use only voices marked as local. If there is none, an alert falls back to a chime and on-screen text.
- Drawing and sound only read Player views and client-only presentation state; they never change the Match (ADR 0002).
- Adding a real asset file later (for example a recorded voice) would reverse this decision and needs its own ADR and a one-way door.
